 Looking For Your Next Binge? Here Are The Best K-Dramas To Watch As The Nights Get Cooler 
 Time to grab some popcorn
 by 
 Samah Tabba 
 Published: Nov 4, 2026 
 SHARE 
 FB TW PIN MAIL 
 There’s nothing quite like settling in for a K-drama binge , especially when the evenings start getting a little cooler . Whether you’re in the mood for a romance that’ll have you kicking your feet, a twisty thriller that’ll keep you guessing or a workplace drama with plenty of chaos, there’s something for every kind of viewer coming up.
 From complicated love stories and unexpected reunions to murder mysteries and high-stakes rivalries, here are the K-dramas to add to your watchlist.
 A Love Other Than Yours
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Prime Video Singapore (@primevideosg) 
 Ten years into their relationship, Namgung Ho (Seo Kang-joon) and Lee Mi-do (Ahn Eun-jin) have reached a crossroads. Once fuelled by the excitement of new love, their relationship has settled into something built on loyalty and familiarity. But when those familiar feelings start to change, the couple are left questioning whether it’s time to call it quits or finally take the next step and get married.
 Ho is a charming assistant manager at a confectionery company, while Mi-do is a film director whose once-promising career has hit a difficult patch. Having stood by each other through life’s ups and downs, can they find their way back to the spark that brought them together?
 A Bona Fide Killer
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by MBC DRAMA official (@mbcdrama_now) 
 What happens when your nine-to-five involves taking out criminals, but your family thinks you have an ordinary office job? Meet Yoo Bo-na (Kong Hyo-jin), a highly skilled assassin known as Kingfisher, who works for a secret organisation targeting particularly heinous criminals. At home, however, she’s simply a wife and mum to a four-year-old daughter.
 After taking three years off for maternity leave, Bo-na returns to the job, only to find that balancing family life with a career in assassination is no easy feat. Things get even more complicated when her journalist husband, Kwon Tae-seong (Jung Joon-won), is assigned to investigate the very killer he doesn’t know he’s married to.
 The Affair Was Just the Beginning
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Viu Philippines (@viuphilippines) 
 A picture-perfect life, a suspicious husband and a family secret that spirals completely out of control? We’re listening. Park Kyung-hee (Kim Hye-soo) appears to have it all, from a successful interior design business to a carefully curated social media presence and a seemingly happy family.
 Hoping to take her business to the next level, she strikes up a friendship with her wealthy neighbour, Soo-jung (Cho Yeo-jeong). But when rumours of her husband’s affair lead Kyung-hee to investigate, she makes a horrifying discovery: he’s disposing of a dead body, and their daughter may be involved in the killing. As the family attempts to cover up what happened, an anonymous message threatens to expose everything. Expect plenty of secrets, blackmail and twists.
 OK! Let’s Get Divorced
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Viu Indonesia (@viuindonesia) 
 Sometimes, love and business really don’t mix. Baek Mi-young (Lee Min-jung) has always dreamed of becoming a tailor, inspired by her father’s work in the trade. After losing her parents, she throws herself into her job at a wedding dress shop, where she meets designer Ji Won-ho (Kim Ji-seok). The two fall in love, get married and eventually build their own company, J&White.
 But seven years into their marriage, things look very different. Their business is on the brink of bankruptcy, and an incident from their fourth year together has left their relationship in crisis. While Mi-young fights to save the company they’ve built, she’s also asking her husband for a divorce. It’s a love story with a rather different question at its centre: what happens when staying together becomes harder than starting over?
 Our Sticky Love
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by MyDramaList Official (@my.drama.list) 
 A fake relationship, a forgotten first love and a little bit of danger? Our Sticky Love has all the ingredients for a binge-worthy romantic comedy. Jang Tae-ha (Jung Hae-in) was once a promising boxer before becoming involved with a gang. Now working as a boxing coach, he’s hoping to leave that life behind for good. There’s just one final mission standing in his way.
 That mission brings him face-to-face with Go Eun-sae (Ha-young), his first love, who no longer remembers him. Eun-sae is a prosecutor investigating a criminal organisation, but after an unexpected accident, she wakes up with no memory of who she is. Tae-ha steps in and tells her that he’s her boyfriend, setting the stage for a reunion that’s anything but straightforward.
 The Ordinary Jackpot
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by HBO Max Singapore (@hbomaxsg) 
 We’ve all wondered what we’d do if we suddenly won the lottery, but Gong Eun-tae (Lee Jun-hyuk) isn’t exactly planning to hand in his notice. After spending his life working towards a quiet, ordinary existence, he finds himself feeling a little underwhelmed by the prospect of a future that looks much the same as his past.
 Then he wins the lottery, taking home a prize of 1.3 billion won. It’s a substantial amount, but not quite enough to completely change his circumstances, so he keeps showing up to work. Still, the unexpected win starts to shift his outlook on life. If you’ve ever fantasised about a lottery win that comes with a side of existential crisis, this one’s for you.
 Made in Korea 2
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Disney+ Singapore (@disneyplussg) 
 If you haven’t watched Made in Korea yet, consider this your sign to catch up. The crime thriller became Disney+ and Hulu’s most-watched Korean original last year, and it’s back for a second season with even more suspense, power struggles and underground dealings.
 The first season followed Baek Kitae, a Korean Central Intelligence Agency (KCIA) official leading a secret double life as the head of an underground drug network, and Jang Geonyoung, a determined prosecutor intent on bringing him down. Season two jumps nine years ahead to 1979, with Kitae more powerful and wealthy than ever, continuing to balance his life as a government agent with his criminal operation.
 The Scandal
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by All Cinema Verse 🎥 (@allcinemaverse) 
 Set during the Joseon era, The Scandal follows Lady Cho (Son Ye-jin), a clever and captivating woman who is frustrated by the restrictions society places on her. Determined to challenge the rules that limit her, she proposes a game of seduction to her admirer, Cho Won (Ji Chang-wook), a charming man who has never been particularly interested in love.
 He accepts the challenge in an attempt to win her heart, but things become more complicated when he approaches An Hui-yeon (Nana), a widow who has vowed to remain faithful to her late husband. As attraction and conflicting emotions enter the picture, the game begins to take on a life of its own. Think period costumes, complicated relationships and plenty of romantic tension.
 Four Hands, Two Sonatas
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Netflix Philippines (@netflixph) 
 For anyone who loves a coming-of-age story, Four Hands, Two Sonatas follows a group of talented young musicians as they navigate friendship, love and competition at Korea Arts High School.
 At the centre of the story are two gifted pianists: perfectionist Kang Pi-o (Song Kang), who’s used to coming first, and Choi Jeong-yo (Lee Jun-young), a prodigy whose difficult circumstances have kept him from recognising his own talent. When their paths cross, their musical worlds are turned upside down. With viola student Hong Jae-in (Jang Gyu-ri) also in the mix, the series explores the highs and lows of growing up alongside people who challenge and inspire you.
 My Bias, My Boss
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by HBO Max Singapore (@hbomaxsg) 
 If you’ve ever had a celebrity crush, imagine finding out your favourite idol is also your colleague. That’s the situation facing Nam Da-reum (Kim Hye-jun), who’s spent 11 years as a devoted fan of idol-turned-actor Lee Chan (Cha Woo-min). She even turns down an offer from a major company to work at Appello, the fashion start-up where he now holds a director position.
 But her new job comes with an unexpected complication: the company’s CEO, Kang Ha-gi (Kang Hoon), whose cool exterior hides a much warmer personality. As Da-reum’s professional life gets increasingly tangled up with her personal admiration for Chan, she finds herself caught between the life she’s dreamed of and the people she actually works with.
 Flex X Cop 2
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Disney+ Singapore (@disneyplussg) 
 Rich kid turned detective Jin I-soo (Ahn Bo-hyun) is back for another round of crime-solving. After discovering that he genuinely enjoys police work, I-soo completes his formal training at the police academy and returns to the violent crimes team, ready to put his skills to the test.
 But his return isn’t exactly smooth sailing. Joo Hye-ra (Jung Eun-chae), the instructor who made his academy days particularly difficult, arrives as the team’s new leader. With a new dynamic in the department and more cases to tackle, the second season promises another mix of action, mystery and workplace tension.
 Mousetrap
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Netflix Indonesia (@netflixid) 
 For something a little darker, Mousetrap is a thriller about losing absolutely everything — including your identity. Je Moon-jae (Ryu Jun-yeol) is a reclusive novelist whose carefully contained life takes a terrifying turn when his fingerprint no longer unlocks his phone and the friend who once handled everything for him suddenly disappears.
 He soon discovers that someone known as Rat has taken his name, identity and property, leaving him with no way to prove who he is. Desperate to get his life back, Moon-jae turns to Noja (Sul Kyung-gu), a dangerous loan shark who runs a private detective agency. But Noja has his own reasons for getting involved: Moon-jae owes him money, and he’s been searching for him for three years. A mysterious identity thief, a missing friend and a rather questionable detective make this one for thriller fans.
 Okay, but if you’re into swoon-worthy moments, here are other K-dramas to watch rn.
